page.layout: One page of text, full width. Below the running text: an indented italic verse stanza, then the word FINIS centred. At the lower right, the catchword EPI-.

main_text.p: cietate fœlicissimas. Quæ ut arctius coalescerent, diffidio opus fuisse videtur ut ex belli dispendiis pa-cis compendia pernoscerent, eamque posthac im-pensius colerent, perinde ut nusquam lætior dies quam ubi tristes nebulas solis radii dispulere. Qui vero innoxiorum ruinas improba spe præceperant, ac ferro & flamma per summam immanitatem omnia involvere satagebant, semperque obnitebantur ne concordia coalescerent, ecce rebus aliter jam flu-entibus, quam amaram rerum vicissitudinem expe-riuntur! ἐχθρὸν[?] illud ὥμμα[?] vivit & vigilat, justitiæ ille oculus illibatus, hic hic est qui

p.i: Funesta belli incendia sustulit[?]: Fregit cruentæ spicula lanceæ: Contrivit arcus, & volucres In cinerem minuit quadrigas.

page.notes: The verse stanza is set in italic and indented; its lines are run together into one paragraph. "sustulit" is read with some doubt because the long s and f are hard to tell apart at this scan resolution. The two Greek words "ἐχθρὸν" and "ὥμμα" are read from a small, faded print and are marked [?]. The catchword "EPI-" sits at the right below the last line and keeps its printed hyphen. No marginal notes are printed on this page.
